newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sentences six Chinese mutineers to death.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sentences six Chinese mutineers to death.

text.p: A South Korean court on Tuesday sentenced to death six mainland Chinese seamen of Korean descent for murdering the captain of a Korean fishing vessel and 10 crew members, a court official said.
The six were sentenced in the southern port city of Pusan.

The South Korean captain of the tuna boat was murdered along with three Indonesians, six other Koreans and an ethnic Korean Chinese in a mutiny in the South Pacific apparently sparked by harsh working conditions.
In addition to the mutineers, one South Korean navigator and six Indonesians survived the tragedy in August.
The mutineers dumped the bodies overboard. The crime came to light when Japanese maritime police found the Pescamar No. 15 drifting without fuel south of Japan.
The court official said all six defendants had confessed to the killings during the trial. It was not known if they would appeal the sentences.

The mutiny occurred after the captain radioed that he was heading for Samoa in the South Pacific to replace rebellious crewmen. Police said the Honduras-registered, 254-gross-ton vessel was later heading for China when its engines stopped.
South Korea's deep sea fishing fleet has been hiring increasing numbers of foreign crew because of spiralling wages at home.
